source.stem: The diagram shows a quadrilateral on a 1 cm² grid.

parts.text: Write down the mathematical name of this quadrilateral. [1]
Work out the area of this quadrilateral. Give the units of your answer. [3]

hinge.title: Connect triangular-number dot patterns to square-number dot patterns.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Square number is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Connect triangular-number dot patterns to square-number dot patterns' is answered as square number rather than triangular number.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Square number is what produces triangular number, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Connect triangular-number dot patterns to square-number.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is triangular number because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Connect triangular-number dot patterns to square-number dot patterns' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: triangular number is settled by running 'Decide which locker numbers are touched exactly twice': A locker is touched exactly twice when its number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself — on the item about Connect triangular-number dot patterns to square-number.

intelligence.enrichment: A square dot array can be viewed as two adjacent triangular-number parts, so extending the triangular pattern also extends the related square pattern.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Mathematics question. Chapter: math/grade_08/ch_101. The student must decide: Connect triangular-number dot patterns to square-number dot patterns. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Supply exactly one complete tikzpicture. The stem must refer to that figure. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options)
